Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):
  • Low mood, loss of energy and appetite for ~3.5 months  
  • Unintentional weight loss ≈1 stone over ~6 months  
  • Nausea without vomiting; no diarrhea, blood, or mucus in stool  
  • Episodic palpitations and perceived shortness of breath mainly in elevators; no dyspnea on walking a mile; no chest pain  
  • History of hypothyroidism; patient ceased thyroxine (date unspecified)  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes): Not recorded.  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines: Previously on thyroxine; currently not taking it (dose/route/frequency not documented). No other medications reported.  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus): Not recorded.  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks: Decreased libido/“nightly activities” per spouse; no further details.  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:  
  • Physical activity markedly reduced (“haven’t been walking lately”)  
  • Diet: poor appetite; no other dietary details  
  • Tobacco, alcohol, other substances: Not recorded.  
- Hearing and vision concerns: Not recorded.  
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm): Reports feeling “down,” low mood; reluctant to label as depression. No suicidal ideation disclosed. Possible anxiety episodes with palpitations in elevators.  
- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors: Married; works as a lawyer; recent job change (~3 months) may coincide with symptom onset. No housing or financial concerns reported.

Examination

- Vital signs: BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded.  
- Anthropometry: height, weight, BMI, waist circumference if indicated: Not recorded (patient reports ~1 stone weight loss).  
- Oral health: gums, teeth, dentures if relevant: Not recorded.  
- Ear exam including otoscopy: Not performed.  
- Eye exam: visual acuity, pupil response, fundus if indicated: Not performed.  
- Urinalysis: dipstick for protein, glucose, ketones, blood: Not performed.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Blood tests planned: Full blood count, renal function, liver function, thyroid function, vitamin levels; assess for anemia.  
- Additional tests discussed: None specified, but clinician advised ECG/physical exam if indicated after results.  
- Other age-appropriate screenings (cervical, mammography, FOBT, DEXA): Not applicable or not discussed.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification: Advised to seek urgent care for new chest pain or bowel changes. No specific lifestyle counselling documented.  
- Discuss patient health goals and priorities: Not recorded.  
- Assess eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA): Not recorded.  
- Referral to allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports: Not recorded.  
- Schedule follow-up and recall appointments as needed: Patient to arrange blood tests via support line; follow-up appointment after results.  

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral  
- Specialist referral (endocrinology) if thyroid dysfunction confirmed or symptoms persist  
- ECG or cardiology review if palpitations continue or escalate  
- Lifestyle support for physical inactivity and nutrition  

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: vitals, BMI, waist circumference, immunisation review, smoking/alcohol status, detailed cardiovascular risk assessment, urinalysis, formal mental health screening.  
● Internal conflicts or contradictions: Hypothyroidism history yet experiencing weight loss and palpitations (could indicate hyperthyroidism or other etiology); patient reports able to walk a mile without dyspnea yet also states not walking lately—limited activity level vs stated tolerance.  
● Transcript quality notes: Audio clear; age in transcript (35 y) does not match assessment template for ≥55 y adults; many routine preventive elements were not addressed during consult.
